new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is stated anywhere. Foley reports, from Konel's short handwritten wordlist, that Kembra is tonal (one high/low minimal pair on ya) and says nothing about stress or accent placement. Usher's relay of the same wordlist shows acute marks on a few forms (ja, kia, nokwa, amagrei, ugilo, utuos) whose meaning (tone vs stress) is not explained.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the data base is a single short prephonemic wordlist plus six sentences.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms from a wordlist; the subject of the 'tonal' sentence is cut off in the snippet (probably 'The language is' or similar).
new_statements.identity_note: Kembra of Kiambra village, Kaisenar District, Keerom Regency (glottocode kemb1250, ISO xkw); Foley 2018 treats it as an isolate (sec. 4.9) while Usher (New Guinea World) puts it under Lepki-Murkim within South Pauwasi River. All published data derive from one short handwritten wordlist (Konel n.d.); no dialects are distinguished.
